theory: Qualify the reciprocal rule and tangent-gradient statement by requiring an existing inverse branch and a finite nonzero original derivative at the corresponding interior point. The zero-derivative vertical-tangent statement also requires an existing suitable inverse branch; zero derivative alone does not ensure one, as the turning-point cubics demonstrate.
